Comprehensive Review of the plus R Package

1) Algorithm Understanding (PLUS Core)

Methodology Implemented

The package implements an iterative PU-learning (Positive and Unlabeled learning) procedure on top of penalized logistic regression (glmnet::cv.glmnet) with binomial family (R/plus.R:46-53, DESCRIPTION:7).

The core idea in code:

  1. Treat known positives as fixed (valid.id <- which(y == 1)) and others as unlabeled/invalid (R/plus.R:27,31).
  2. Iteratively sample unlabeled cases (roughly balanced to positives), train CV logistic model on positives + sampled unlabeled (R/plus.R:39,46-53).
  3. Predict all rows, derive a positive quantile cutoff from positive predictions (qq) (R/plus.R:55-57).
  4. Rescale around cutoff and squash via sigmoid (1/(1+exp(-10*...))) (R/plus.R:60-64).
  5. Update pseudo-label probabilities and stochastically relabel sampled unlabeled via Bernoulli draws (rbinom) (R/plus.R:69-74).
  6. Stop when sampling weights depleted or label changes stabilize (R/plus.R:76-88).
  7. Fit final CV logistic model on full relabeled data and store outputs in class plus (R/plus.R:92-105, R/new_plus.R:29-36).

Mathematical / Statistical Foundations Visible in Code

  • Penalized logistic regression with elastic-net mixing alpha (R/plus.R:48).
  • PU relabeling loop with stochastic EM-like updates (probability update + Bernoulli sampling) (R/plus.R:69-74).
  • Thresholding by positive quantile (qq) for calibration to known-positive score distribution (R/plus.R:57).
  • AUC metric support via concordance (survival::concordance) (R/auc.R:21-22).

Data Flow Through Package API

  • Fit: plus(x, y) → returns S3 class "plus" with:
    • $plus (cv.glmnet object),
    • $pred_y, $cutoff, $predicted_coefficients, $call (R/new_plus.R:30-35, R/validate_plus.R:18-21).
  • Predict: predict.plus() gives response/class (R/predict.plus.R:34-55).
  • Evaluate: assess.plus(), get_auc.plus(), get_predictions() (R/assess.plus.R:30-57, R/get_auc.R:29-41, R/get_predictions.R:27-49).

3) Enhancement Opportunities

High-Priority Correctness / API Issues

  1. predict.plus docs vs implementation mismatch Docs claim support for link, coefficients, nonzero, etc., but implementation only handles response and class (R/predict.plus.R:15-20, R/predict.plus.R:50-55).

  2. s = "lambda.1se" likely broken match.arg(s) has no explicit choices; formal default only includes "lambda.min" (R/predict.plus.R:34,38).

  3. AUC helper logic is questionable auc_matrix() reconstructs labels as balanced 0/1 ignoring actual rowwise class content in y (R/auc_matrix.R:22-24).

  4. Evaluation utility name suggests CV but uses 1 fold foldid = rep(1, nrowy) so no actual fold split in plus_cv_lognet() (R/plus_cv_lognet.R:33,45).

Quality / Documentation Gaps

  • No tests; no vignettes (none found via directory scan).
  • Numerous typos and doc issues (e.g., “pluse”, “consturctor”, “retrived”) in Rd/R docs (e.g. man/predict.plus.Rd:13, man/fit_plus_example.Rd:6).
  • README has malformed heading escape (\## Example) (README.md:32).
  • Pkgdown site appears stale at version 0.0.1 while DESCRIPTION is 1.0.0 (docs/index.html:36, DESCRIPTION:3).

Performance / Design Opportunities

  • Main loop can run up to 10,000 iterations with repeated cv.glmnet fits (heavy) (R/plus.R:37,46).
  • No exposed controls for max_iter, nfolds, seed/reproducibility, convergence diagnostics.
  • Missing S3 methods: No summary.plus, plot.plus, confusion-matrix utility, calibration curves.
  • Limited input validation in plus() (binary checks, NA handling, shape checks not explicit).

4) Best Usage Patterns

Current Intended Use

  • Intended for binary PU contexts with known positives and unlabeled negatives; especially unbalanced/sparse settings (README.Rmd:31-43, R/plus.R:27-33).
  • Practical flow:
    1. fit <- plus(x_train, y_train) (README.Rmd:67)
    2. predict(fit, newx=...) (README.Rmd:68)
    3. get_auc(...) / assess(...) (README.Rmd:86,90)
  • Text-mining framing is suggested by included abstract datasets (lacs, lacsSample) and DESCRIPTION statement on text analysis helpers (DESCRIPTION:8, R/lacs.R:1-4).

User-Friendliness Improvements

  • Add formula interface.
  • Stronger checks/errors.
  • Explicit class labels semantics.
  • Robust predict types.
  • Reproducibility controls (seed parameter).

5) Rebranding Impact: plus → xplus

Below are all places that would need rename/update.

A) Core Package Identity

File Lines What to Change
DESCRIPTION Lines 1, 22 Package name and URL
_pkgdown.yml Line 1 URL
README.md Lines 4, 25, 37 Title, install, library calls
README.Rmd Lines 16, 39, 49 Title, install, library calls

B) API / Class Names Tightly Coupled to plus

  • Function names: plus, new_plus, validate_plus, plus_cv_lognet, data object names like fit_plus_example, plus_object_example.
  • S3 class "plus" and methods predict.plus, print.plus, assess.plus, get_auc.plus (R/new_plus.R:35, R/predict.plus.R:34, NAMESPACE:3-6,8,12,15).
  • Internal list field object$plus appears in prediction/printing code (R/predict.plus.R:39,47, R/print.plus.R:19,22).

C) Documentation Artifacts

  • All affected man/*.Rd files (names and text), e.g.:
    • man/plus.Rd, man/predict.plus.Rd, man/print.plus.Rd, man/new_plus.Rd, man/plus_cv_lognet.Rd, etc. (man/plus.Rd:3-4, man/predict.plus.Rd:3-4).
  • NAMESPACE regenerated from roxygen after renaming methods/classes (NAMESPACE:1).

D) Website / Build Outputs

  • docs/ generated site embeds package name in titles/nav/citation:
    • docs/index.html:8,35,59,67,70
    • docs/reference/index.html:2,19,85,97
    • docs/authors.html:2,19,56,60
  • After rename, pkgdown should be rebuilt to regenerate docs/.

E) File / Path Names Containing plus

Many filenames include plus and should be reviewed for consistency:

  • R/plus.R, R/predict.plus.R, R/print.plus.R, R/assess.plus.R, etc.
  • man/plus.Rd, man/predict.plus.Rd, …
  • plus.Rproj (optional rename for developer ergonomics).

F) CRAN / Compliance Considerations for Renaming

  • New name xplus is syntactically valid (starts with letter, lowercase style common).
  • Must ensure CRAN name availability separately.
  • License currently GPL (>=3), acceptable as-is (DESCRIPTION:9).
  • Note: LICENSE.md includes ordinary English “plus” usage not related to package naming (e.g. LICENSE.md:399); should not be blindly replaced.
